candidates.title: Diffusion-enhanced GFlowNet for solving vehicle routing problems
candidates.abstract: Traditional neural solvers for solving vehicle routing problems (VRPs) often suffer from limited solution diversity, motivating the development of Generative Flow Network (GFlowNet)–based models. However, the effectiveness of these models is frequently constrained by insufficient flow expansion in high-reward regions, limiting their ability to distribute probability across promising solution routes. The deeper exploration could yield superior results. Diffusion models, in contrast, provide stronger structural guidance for exploration. These two paradigms are naturally complementary: GFlowNet can supply edge-level signals for diffusion to embed, while diffusion can guide broader exploration. Leveraging this synergy, we propose Diffusion-Enhanced GFlowNet (DEG), a novel framework that integrates GFlowNet with a diffusion model to encourage richer flow expansion toward highreward regions and derive higher-quality solutions. Specifically, DEG exploits GFlowNet’s inherent diversity to generate edge-specific backward signals, applies the stochastic noise schedule of diffusion to perturb these signals, and then denoises them within the GFlowNet paradigm. To further improve scalability, we introduce a specialized decoder capable of dynamically adapting to diverse problem scales. Extensive experimental evaluations on synthetic and real-world datasets, including instances with up to 10,000 nodes, demonstrate that DEG consistently achieves favorable performance compared to baseline methods. The code is available at https://github.com/ZHANG-NI/DEG.

candidates.title: Comparative Evaluation of Hyperparameter Optimization Strategies for k-Nearest Neighbors over Mixed Domain Search Spaces
candidates.abstract: k-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) remains a strong baseline due to its simplicity, interpretability, and non-parametric structure; however, its predictive performance is highly sensitive to interacting hyperparameters. This paper studies search-constrained hyperparameter optimization for KNN over a mixed search space comprising an integer neighborhood size, a categorical distance metric, and a continuous Minkowski exponent. Seven tuning strategies are compared under a unified nested validation protocol with standardized preprocessing: grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization, genetic algorithm, surrogate optimization, particle swarm optimization, and grey wolf optimizer. Experiments on diverse public classification datasets from UCI, OpenML, and Kaggle evaluate predictive performance (accuracy, macro-AUC, cross-entropy), validation loss, and runtime. The results indicate that adaptive optimizers generally provide more favorable performancecost trade-offs than exhaustive grids under limited evaluations, while no single method is uniformly best across all datasets. Rank-based statistical comparisons using non-parametric tests further support the observed differences and motivate practical recommendations for selecting tuning strategies as a function of evaluation search and mixed-domain search-space characteristics.

candidates.title: SCRIPT: Scalable Diffusion Policy with Multi-stage Training for Language-driven Physics-Based Humanoid Control
candidates.abstract: Controlling physics-based humanoids from natural-language instructions is a critical step toward general-purpose embodied agents. However, existing methods remain constrained by a tension between semantic expressiveness and physical feasibility, often failing to jointly achieve faithful instruction following, high-quality motion, and stable long-horizon control. We propose SCRIPT, a scalable diffusion policy with a multi-stage training framework for language-driven physics-based humanoid control. The core of SCRIPT is a Joint Action-State-Text Diffusion Transformer (JAST-DiT), which represents actions, physical states, and text as dedicated token streams and couples them through joint attention, enabling direct interaction between language semantics and control dynamics. To stabilize autoregressive control, we introduce a nonlinear history conditioning mechanism, which preserves the dense recent context and samples increasingly sparse cues from long-term history. Beyond supervised imitation pre-training, we propose a post-training stage, further improving the performance using Reinforcement Learning with Hybrid Rewards (RLHR). By injecting learnable noise into the flow-sampling process, RLHR effectively improves motion quality and instruction following within closed-loop simulations using hybrid physical feedback and text rewards. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that SCRIPT outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods, with gains across text alignment, motion quality, and physical realism metrics. Furthermore, scaling studies on the 1200-hour MotionMillion dataset demonstrate consistent performance gains with model scaling, highlighting SCRIPT’s robust scalability for large-scale pre-training. Code and data for this paper are available at https://zhanglele12138.github.io/SCRIPT/.

candidates.title: Adversarial Graph Neural Diffusion for Zero-Day Network Anomaly Detection: A Controlled Evaluation
candidates.abstract: Zero-day intrusions cannot be matched against signatures, so a detector must judge whether a host is behaving abnormally rather than whether it matches a known attack.Continuous-depth graph neural networks that treat message passing as a diffusion process have advanced node classification, and this paper asks whether they transfer to host-level anomaly detection.We present AGND, which combines graph neural diffusion with a time-aware attention operator whose diffusivity decays with the time since two hosts last communicated, and with an adversarial generator that synthesises pseudo-anomalous behaviour.On a controlled benchmark of 1440 windows, 100 hosts and 140 attack episodes from six unseen families, evaluated over 10 independently generated networks, AGND reaches 0.939 AUC-ROC and 0.270 AUC-PR under the original protocol and 0.937 and 0.254 under the corrected protocol of attack-free training and label-free selection.Neither proposed component changes this, and removing the diffusion raises AUC-PR to 0.352 and 0.307 respectively.Isolation forests and one-class support vector machines on the same features exceed every graph model on AUC-PR and a two-layer autoencoder matches the best of them, and the ordering survives training on attack-free windows only, label-free model selection and family-held-out selection.A factorial ablation shows that two hand-engineered relational summaries, not learned graph context, carry the relational signal: without them every method loses between 35 and 60 per cent of its AUC-PR, graph models included.Sweeps of depth, source weight and horizon over all networks show that a single Euler step matches the discrete model, that the loss appears at the second step together with a drop in Dirichlet energy, and that changing the energy through the horizon alone leaves detection quality unchanged, so oversmoothing is part of the mechanism rather than the whole of it.A host-window experiment on CIC-IDS2017 traffic reproduces the absence of a graph advantage but not the diffusion penalty.We report a negative result with a bounded explanation.

candidates.title: Convoluted Support Matrix Machine in High Dimensions
candidates.abstract: The Support Vector Machine (SVM) has been effective in various discrimination problems.Recently, there has been growing interest in extending the traditional vector-based SVM to accommodate structured matrix inputs.However, the nonsmooth hinge loss poses significant challenges for both theoretical and computational development.To address these issues, we propose a convex smoothing procedure for the hinge loss.Additionally, we introduce an elastic-net type penalty to handle high-dimensional matrix inputs.Our approach surpasses the standard SVM for discrimination involving high-dimensional matrix inputs.The proposed method provably achieves an optimal statistical convergence rate, and the smooth, convex loss function enables the development of a highly efficient optimization algorithm.This algorithm features a fast linear convergence rate and a simple implementation.Extensive simulations and an electroencephalography application demonstrate the method's superiority in classification accuracy and computational efficiency.

candidates.title: Investigation and Optimization of Air Pollution Risk by a Multi-criteria Decision Making Method Using Fuzzy TOPSIS: A Case Study of Construction Workers
candidates.abstract: Background: Investigating human health during work importantly affect the safety and efficiency of the society. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Methods: The comparison matrices (binary) and the Phillips–Perron test of different criteria and sub-criteria of health risk, including safety view, safety efficiency, understanding the risk, and risk investigation, were assessed to find the most influential factors for the optimization of the health risk of the workers. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. However, among the sub-criteria, the most effective ones were “worker knowledge”, “manager knowledge”, “logistic specialized managers”, “modern facilities”, and “modern technology”. The selection of the linear and non-linear models was conducted according to the F values, and the model parameters were estimated using the Newton-Raphson test. Most coefficients were significant at P= 0.99. The model also has a high describing value of 0.97. The final estimated homogeneity coefficient was equal to 1.31, and it ranged from 0.86 to 2.72 for the critical risk investigation. The significance of the present research is to increase the health and safety of workers during work resulting in a more sustainable and healthier environment. Conclusion: Accordingly, the managers could handle the risks, determine the tolerable risks, indicate the risk of each process to control expenses, and take the essential measures for optimization.

candidates.title: Trajectory fit alone does not identify causal edges: a white-box masked ODE benchmark for trans-omics digital twins of drug action mechanisms
candidates.abstract: Dynamic multi-omics models infer drug mechanisms from trajectories, but trajectory accuracy alone cannot verify that learned regulatory edges are mechanistically correct. We asked to what extent fitting time-series dynamics identifies intervenable causal edges across observation and optimization budgets.We built white-box ordinary differential equations with candidate-edge masks for gene-expression, protein, signalling and metabolite dynamics, using a mouse-liver trans-omics topology and ground-truth semi-synthetic time series. Under noise-free,complete, densely sampled data, from-scratch training ranked edges near chance(edge-class area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve, 0.48-0.53); the unattainable oracle-initialized upper bound reached 0.94-0.99 on the same metric.Unobserved layers absorbed error. In ground-truth knockout tests, development-batch endpoint-sign accuracy was 67.9% for one-hop non-convergent targets but 33.3% for two-hop targets. Across tested practical budgets, fitting did not yield reliable edge recovery; trajectory fit alone therefore does not establish mechanistic identification. This benchmark supports mechanistic audits and exploratory per-prediction confidence grading in multi-omics models.

candidates.title: Rayleigh-Quotient-Based Data Classification Method for Machine Learning
candidates.abstract: Inspired by the ability of human ears to distinguish between different kinds of music and the ability of an ancient instrument to play countless beautiful melodies, this paper proposes the Rayleigh-quotient-based data classification method, which implements data classification by selecting an appropriate eigenfunction coordinate system to represent different categories of data and making different categories of data show significant differences in the coordinate components, meanwhile, transforming the selection problem of an eigenfunction coordinate system into a design problem of physical parameters of music instruments, such as designing a non-uniform string or membrane with distributed supports. In theory, the method is based on the eigenvalue problem for Sturm-Liouville differential equation, the eigenvalue problem for functional minimization, and the generalized eigenvalue problem for matrices, which have a time-honored history and can provide strong theoretical foundation and support. In addition, each parameter in the method has a clear physical interpretation and can be adjusted under the guidance of a set of complete theory, and their influence on classification results is definite, avoiding the large time consumption due to randomly adjusting parameters. The data classification procedure is divided into 2 steps, including mass density function design and stiffness function design, which not only simplifies the process of parameter adjustment, but also enables the optimization algorithm to be implemented by the linear programming with a low computational complexity, theoretically guaranteeing a high computational efficiency. Considering the amount of data being classified is large, two kinds of algorithms are developed to implement data classification, where one is a statistical averaging algorithm and the other is an incremental iterative algorithm. Finally, by combining the image database MNIST, the Rayleigh-quotient-based data classification method is employed to build an image classifier, which is trained on the MNIST training set including 60,000 images, and is tested on the MNIST test set including 10,000 images. The classification results show that by selecting an appropriate eigenfunction coordinate system, the Rayleigh quotient distribution of each category of image can be controlled within a very narrow range, while different categories of images show significant difference in the Rayleigh quotient distribution; the classification accuracy on the MNIST training set and on the MNIST test set are stable at about 99.50%, and the maximum accuracy can reach to 100.00% on the MNIST training set and 99.76% on the MNIST test set; and the Rayleigh-quotient threshold can be selected within a very wide range, beneficial for the robustness and stability of data classification.

candidates.title: Targeted protein degradation as a resistance-resilient strategy for antiviral drug discovery.
candidates.abstract: Antiviral drug discovery is constrained by viral evolution, restricted target space and stringent exposure requirements. Targeted protein degradation can eliminate viral proteins or host-dependency factors rather than relying solely on sustained inhibition. Preclinical studies across hepatitis C virus, influenza viruses, flaviviruses, coronaviruses and HIV demonstrate infection-relevant antiviral activity and, in selected cases, activity against inhibitor-resistant variants. Such coverage does not establish resilience to degrader-selected escape. Viral binding changes, nonproductive ternary complexes, tissue exposure and host pathway dependence remain liabilities. We define resistance resilience through matched comparators and propose evidence gates integrating mechanistic controls, variant mapping, laboratory selection, pharmacokinetics and safety.

candidates.title: Biologically Guided Deep Learning for Personalized PSA Forecasting in Intermittent Prostate Cancer Therapy
candidates.abstract: Intermittent Androgen Deprivation Therapy (IADT) offers a promising management strategy for prostate cancer by alternating treatment periods with the aim of delaying castration resistance and mitigating side effects. An evolutionary rationale for treatment interruptions is to preserve treatment-sensitive cells that may competitively suppress resistant populations. However, designing optimal patient-specific treatment schedules remains challenging due to the complex dynamics of tumor evolution and the computational intensity of traditional mechanistic simulation models. Standard mathematical models have prespecified structures that may inadequately capture patient-specific tumor evolution, limiting Prostate Specific Antigen (PSA) forecasting accuracy and adaptation to new patient data. These limitations may reduce the effectiveness of treatment policies learned using these models. To address them, we present a domain-adapted machine learning framework that integrates biological constraints into the deep learning architecture and embeds historical biomarkers to act as a robust, computationally efficient neural surrogate for mechanistic simulations. This framework enhances generalization across sparse clinical profiles by leveraging deep neural representations for patient-specific and cross-patient parameter learning, and potentially enables the identification of personalized dosing schedules tailored to individual tumor trajectories. Preliminary evaluations confirm that it reliably captures treatment-associated PSA dynamics while overcoming the computational bottlenecks of numerical solvers. Ultimately, this work provides a scalable foundation for optimizing adaptive therapy protocols to extend time to disease progression. We present the architectural formulation, forecasting evaluation against mechanistic baselines, and training and optimization procedures of the deep neural networks.

candidates.title: Beyond LLM Serving: Characterizing Vision-Language-Action Workloads for Embodied AI System Design
candidates.abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models translate multimodal observations into low-level robot actions. During robot operation, each control period sets an inference deadline, and overruns leave the robot acting on stale observations, reducing task success. Meeting this deadline motivates on-device or nearby edge execution, where a single robot requires batch-1 inference outside the design point of LLM serving systems. Although VLA architectures combine familiar vision-language, autoregressive, and diffusion-style components, their runtime behavior in this batch-1 control setting remains uncharacterized. We characterize four representative VLA models on an edge GPU server and two onboard SoCs, using single-inference profiling and 43,200 closed-loop episodes. Action tensor dimensionality determines whether a stage is memory- or compute-bound, platform balance can shift that bottleneck, and GPU frequency scaling yields a platform-dependent energy-latency sweet spot. In closed-loop operation, overlapping inference with action execution creates an accuracy-speed-energy tradeoff, and no configuration is Pareto-dominant across deployment SLOs. These results guide joint design of VLA model architectures, hardware, and runtime policies.

candidates.title: Improving Target-Adverse Event Association Prediction via Inverse Node Frequency Transformation to Mitigate Knowledge Graph Topological Bias
candidates.abstract: Motivation: Identifying significant associations between therapeutic protein targets and adverse events (AEs) is a critical component of drug safety assessment. To accelerate the process, machine learning methods have been developed to predict these associations as edges in network data integrating molecular interactions and other key biomedical knowledge. However, these networks often suffer from topological imbalances where a minority of "hub" nodes determine the predictive signal. This "topological" or "degree bias" can lead to poor performance on novel or understudied targets where safety inference is most needed. Results: We introduce Inverse Node Frequency (INF), a generally applicable node degree-based approach for mitigating topological bias. Employing an enriched biomedical knowledge graph and our own carefully curated target-adverse event associations, we apply INF as a normalisation procedure on a class of graph-derived features called metapaths and evaluate their resulting target-AE association prediction performance. Our results demonstrate that INF significantly improves the true positive rate (TPR/recall) for low-degree targets compared to the untransformed metapath features as well as a popular established normalisation method, while also achieving highly competitive hits@k, a ranking-based metric for knowledge graph-based inference. We also evaluated INF on an external set of target-AE associations never before used for modelling, on which INF also showed superior resilience compared to the two benchmarks.

candidates.title: KAIROS: Stateful, Context-Aware Power-Efficient Agentic Inference Serving
candidates.abstract: Power has become a central bottleneck for AI inference. This problem is becoming more urgent as agentic AI emerges as a major workload class, yet prior power-management techniques focus almost entirely on single-turn LLM serving. Our analysis shows that agentic serving behaves fundamentally differently: each request carries long-lived context that evolves across tool-interleaved turns, and lowering GPU frequency can push the system into a thrashing regime where memory pressure sharply worsens both performance and power efficiency. These observations show that power optimization for agentic serving requires rethinking. We present KAIROS, a context-aware power optimization system for agentic AI serving. KAIROS uses agent context as a first-class control signal to jointly manage GPU frequency, per-instance concurrency, and multi-instance request placement. This enables KAIROS to save power when memory headroom exists while avoiding thrashing and preserving performance targets. At a high level, KAIROS tracks requests at agent granularity, adapts local control to context growth and agent progress, and routes agents across instances to jointly improve power efficiency and memory stability. Evaluated across diverse software and data engineering agentic tasks, KAIROS achieves an average of 27% (up to 39.8%) power reduction while meeting the performance targets.

candidates.title: Empirical Risk Minimization for Losses without Variance
candidates.abstract: This paper considers an empirical risk minimization problem under heavy-tailed settings, where data does not have finite variance, but only has (1 + ε)-th moment with ε ∈ (0, 1).Instead of using an estimation procedure based on truncated observed data, we choose the optimizer by minimizing the risk value.Those risk values can be robustly estimated via using the remarkable Catoni's method.Thanks to the structure of Catoni-type influence functions, we are able to establish excess risk upper bounds via using generalized generic chaining methods.Moreover, we take computational issues into consideration.We especially theoretically investigate two types of optimization methods, robust gradient descent algorithm and empirical risk-based methods.With an extensive numerical study, we find that the optimizer based on empirical risks via Catoni-style estimation indeed shows better performance than other baselines.It indicates that estimation directly based on truncated data may lead to unsatisfactory results.

candidates.title: Daily-Academic: A Semantic Literature Discovery and Journal Tracking Platform for Biomedical Research
candidates.abstract: Objective: Biomedical researchers monitoring newly published literature rely on fragmented combinations of keyword alerts, manual database searches, journal subscriptions and repository portals. We aimed to develop and evaluate an integrated platform that unifies semantic literature discovery, journal monitoring and linked omics dataset exploration within a single researcher-oriented workflow, driven by a user profile that remains explicit and editable. Methods: Daily-Academic aggregates publication metadata from biomedical literature repositories and public omics resources and encodes titles and abstracts as dense semantic representations to support similarity-based retrieval beyond keyword matching. Recommendations are ranked by combining semantic relevance to the user profile with publication recency and journal-level preferences. The profile is derived from three user-supplied signals: a free-text statement of research interests, an optional link to the user's own publication record, and interaction history. Retrieval quality was assessed on an offline benchmark of 30 biomedical queries over a fixed corpus of 259,246 publications, comparing Daily-Academic with a lexical BM25 baseline and a PubMedBERT bi-encoder under pooled assessment with graded relevance judgements. candidates.title: Optimization Dispatch Strategy for Interconnected Shared Energy Storage Systems in Distribution Transformers Based on Regional Dynamic Partitioning
candidates.abstract: To address the operational volatility and complexity caused by the high penetration of renewable energy in distribution networks, the traditional static and isolated operation mode of distribution transformers struggles to simultaneously ensure power supply quality and economic efficiency. This paper proposes a coordinated dispatch strategy for interconnected distribution transformers based on regional dynamic partitioning and shared energy storage systems. Firstly, an improved K-means partitioning model for distribution transformers is constructed. By integrating a comprehensive distance metric that combines load characteristics and geospatial information, the limitations of traditional single-dimensional partitioning are overcome. Furthermore, a bi-level optimization dispatch model is established, with the upper-level objective of minimizing voltage deviation and the lower-level objective of minimizing operational cost, achieving the coordinated optimization of power quality and economic operation. On this basis, a comprehensive evaluation index composed of voltage stability and economic efficiency is innovatively proposed, and a dynamic weight adjustment mechanism feedback-based on the electrical correlation degree of distribution transformers is designed. This mechanism drives the closed-loop dynamic optimization of the partitioning scheme, enabling it to adaptively respond to the spatiotemporal changes of loads and renewable energy. Simulation results show that the proposed strategy increases the renewable energy utilization rate of distribution transformers by 5% and the daily maximum energy storage utilization rate by 9%, while forming a reasonable partitioning scheme with geographical compactness and electrical tightness.

candidates.title: PhageLysClass: Evidence-aware classification of phage lytic proteins using protein language models
candidates.abstract: Phage lytic proteins are promising antibacterial and biotechnological candidates, yet uncertain annotations, modular architectures, and class imbalance complicate sequence-based classification. We developed PhageLysClass, an evidence-aware framework for recognizing lytic proteins and distinguishing Endolysins, Depolymerases, and virion-associated lytic enzymes. From 442,329 unique phage sequences, including 11,867 evidence-supported positives, we defined distinct candidate non-target, unlabeled, and challenge populations. Seven supervised and two positive-unlabeled tasks were evaluated across factorial redundancy and train-test homology conditions, yielding 2,240 and 768 experiments, respectively. Redundancy reduction influenced generalization more strongly than homology separation, with non-additive interactions between them. ESM2-T30 consistently outperformed alternative representations and supported a hierarchical classifier achieving approximately 0.89 MCC under strict R30/S30 conditions in the selected, pre-refitting benchmark. Applied without retraining to 77,897 sequences across three collections, PhageLysClass combined predictions with physicochemical and geometric contextualization, highlighting Depolymerase-like candidates among structurally ambiguous proteins while distinguishing reference-supported assignments from extrapolation.

candidates.title: AI-driven multi-omics identifies SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages as a therapeutic target and predicts lymph node metastasis in papillary thyroid cancer.
candidates.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming drug design by enabling the systematic discovery of therapeutic targets and the prediction of drug response from complex biomedical data. In papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), lymph node metastasis remains a key determinant of poor outcome, yet targetable drivers and predictive models for metastasis are lacking. Here, we integrate single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and machine learning to identify SPP1⁺ tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) as a functionally validated driver of lymph node metastasis in PTC. Using single-cell and spatial analyses, we show that SPP1⁺ TAMs engage TM4SF1⁺ malignant epithelial cells via the SPP1-CD44 axis within a hypoxic niche, driving tumor stemness, invasion, and metastatic progression. SPP1⁺ TAMs exhibit a hypoxic, M2-polarized phenotype and their abundance correlates with worse overall and progression‑free survival in metastatic PTC patients. We further develop an integrative machine-learning model based on SPP1⁺ TAM‑derived molecular features that predicts lymph node status with high accuracy. Preclinically, pharmacological targeting of SPP1 attenuates tumor cell migration, invasion, and lung metastasis, supporting its candidacy as a therapeutic target. Collectively, this study demonstrates how AI‑driven multi‑omics analysis can jointly identify a functionally validated target and generate a clinically deployable predictive model, illustrating a framework for bridging computational discovery with translational oncology.

candidates.title: Affibody-conjugated hyaluronic acid hydrogels within collagen sponges enhance dose-dependent BMP-2-mediated bone formation and repair of critically sized femoral defects
candidates.abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein-2 (BMP-2) is a potent osteoinductive growth factor; however, its burst release from clinical collagen sponge carriers can cause inflammation and ectopic bone formation. Alternative delivery vehicles slow BMP-2 protein release through increased crosslinking density, which stiffens the polymer network and can restrict cell infiltration required for bone formation. Here, we introduce a BMP-2 delivery system in which a hyaluronic acid (HA) hydrogel containing BMP-2-specific affibodies is formed within clinically used collagen sponges to retain BMP-2 through protein-material affinity interactions rather than physical entrapment. We developed a maleimide functionalized, hydrazone crosslinked HA hydrogel such that affibody conjugation is chemically orthogonal to network formation, allowing affibody density to be varied independently of crosslinking density. Forming this hydrogel within a collagen sponge produced composite scaffolds with improved surgical handling and BMP-2 retention. Moreover, in vitro, composite scaffolds exhibited minimal swelling while retaining more BMP-2 than the collagen sponge alone. In vivo, composite scaffolds conjugated with BMP-2-specific affibodies improved ectopic mineralization in a BMP-2 dose-dependent manner. In a critically sized femoral defect, composite scaffolds with and without affibodies significantly increased bone volume relative to the collagen sponge. Thus, this composite scaffold effectively integrates the clinically used collagen sponge with a tunable HA hydrogel and BMP-2-specific affibodies to improve BMP-2-mediated bone regeneration and expand the use of naturally derived biomaterials for bone healing.

candidates.title: FUSE: FUsing EEG-MEG in a Shared Embedding via self-supervised learning for BCI
candidates.abstract: Combining complementary neurophysiological modalities offers a promising strategy for improving motor imagery (MI) brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), but learning shared representations across modalities remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a two-phase deep learning framework for multimodal EEG-MEG decoding that explicitly decouples representation learning from downstream classification. In the first phase, a convolutional encoder-decoder learns a shared latent representation by predicting the power spectral density (PSD) of EEG and MEG signals directly from time-domain activity, rather than using the conventional objective of reconstructing the input signal. In the second phase, the encoder is frozen and its learned representations are reused, without further adaptation, to perform the classification of the downstream MI-BCI task. The framework was evaluated on simultaneous EEG and MEG recordings from 20 participants. The learned representations consistently outperformed conventional handcrafted spectral features, increasing median classification accuracy from 0.734 to 0.794. The multimodal framework also improved performance over MEG alone (median accuracy from 0.680 to 0.794) and yielded a modest increase over EEG alone (median accuracy from 0.765 to 0.794), providing a more robust decoding strategy than single-modality approaches. Furthermore, the learned latent representations were transferable across participants, with more than half of cross-subject models performing within 0.01 accuracy of their subject-specific counterparts. These findings demonstrate that task-agnostic representation learning can capture physiologically meaningful multimodal neural representations that remain transferable across individuals, offering a promising foundation for more robust and reusable BCI pipelines.

candidates.title: scPACE: A Personalized Autoencoder for Cell Evolution in Single-Cell Transcriptomics
candidates.abstract: Single-cell studies increasingly profile large cohorts of individuals, measuring thousands of cells in each donor. These datasets contain information at two levels: variation among individual cells and among donors. Analyzing both levels requires methods that can learn cellular representations, infer cell and donor states, and account for cell types that may be missing in some donors. Existing methods partially address these tasks. We introduce scPACE, a hierarchical personalized variational autoencoder handling these tasks. scPACE learns a cell representation, a cell state, and then aggregates cells within each type of cell to infer a donor state. It also imputes missing cell types with confidence estimates. Across simulated cohorts and a developing mouse visual-cortex dataset, scPACE recovered held-out cell and donor states accurately while achieving efficient cell-type imputation and representation. scPACE provides a unified framework for learning phenotypes across cellular and donor scales in cohort-scale single-cell transcriptomics.

candidates.title: Localizing Multivariate CAViaR
candidates.abstract: Risk transmission among financial markets and their participants is time-evolving, especially for extreme risk scenarios.Possibly sudden time variation of such risk structures asks for quantitative techniques that can cope with such situations.Here we present a novel localized multivariate CAViaRtype model to respond to the challenge of time-varying risk contagion.For this purpose, we construct a test for parameter homogeneity with totally datadriven critical values.We prove that these critical values lead to the required confidence level.Based on this test, we propose an estimation procedure that adapts to a possible time-variation of the parameter.A comprehensive simulation study supports the effectiveness of our approach in detecting structural changes in multivariate CAViaR.Finally, when applying for the US and German financial markets, we can trace out the dynamic tail risk spillovers and find that the US market appears to play a dominant role in risk transmissions, especially in volatile market periods.

candidates.title: La diffusion des outils et services e-santé auprès de leurs utilisateurs : l’exemple de « Mon espace santé » en France
candidates.abstract: Les pouvoirs publics souhaitent tirer parti des perspectives offertes par le numérique en santé pour améliorer l’information et la prise en charge des patients tout en luttant contre les inégalités de santé dans les territoires. Cependant, en France, si au cours des quinze dernières années, cette transformation digitale du secteur de la santé s’est particulièrement développée, elle a aussi connu des résultats très variables et parfois encore assez décevants. Pour notamment renforcer et accélérer cette transformation digitale, de nombreux travaux ont décrit en détail les modalités et facteurs favorisant l’adoption et l’appropriation des outils et services numériques en santé. En revanche, beaucoup moins de travaux ont porté leur attention sur la phase de diffusion aux utilisateurs de ces outils et services alors qu’elle détermine significativement leur adoption et appropriation. Pour combler ce manque, à partir de la théorie de la diffusion des innovations, nous proposons d’analyser les modalités de diffusion à ses utilisateurs de l’outil « Mon espace santé » proposé et mis en œuvre par la Caisse nationale d’assurance maladie en France. À partir d’une participation observante au sein des équipes chargées de la diffusion de cet outil, nous décrivons les éléments de diffusion de cette innovation digitale (système social, innovation, canaux de communication, temps). Les résultats de cette analyse nous permettent, dans un premier temps, sur le plan théorique, de proposer un premier cadre d’analyse de la diffusion des innovations digitales en santé. L’application de ce cadre d’analyse nous autorise ensuite une caractérisation des modalités de diffusion de l’innovation digitale en santé « centrée sur l’usager » aux côtés de celles relatives à sa conception déjà très illustrées dans la littérature. Ces modalités sont décrites à travers les principales composantes de la diffusion de « Mon espace santé » (différents rôles de l’usager, canaux de communication utilisés et étapes de diffusion) et trois de ses principes directeurs (usager-acteur, État-plateforme, déploiement incitatif centré sur l’usager). Sur le plan pratique, ces composantes et principes de diffusion représentent autant de pistes d’amélioration de la diffusion des innovations digitales en santé dans le secteur public.

candidates.title: An Infected Cryopreserved Precision-Cut Lung Slice Model for Drug Susceptibility Testing in Pneumocystis murina Pneumonia
candidates.abstract: Precision-cut lung slices (PCLS) preserve native three-dimensional lung architecture and cellular complexity, providing a valuable ex vivo platform for studying pulmonary host-pathogen interactions. However, existing PCLS infection models typically introduce microorganisms into previously uninfected tissue, while fresh PCLS prepared from infected lungs have limited experimental flexibility and scalability. To our knowledge, cryopreserved PCLS generated from lungs with an established in vivo pulmonary infection have not been described. Herein, we evaluated cryopreserved PCLS from mice with established Pneumocystis murina pneumonia (PCP) as an ex vivo platform for infection and therapeutic studies. PCLS were prepared from dexamethasone-immunosuppressed mice with established PCP, rested for 24 h, cryopreserved in a novel freezing medium for 12 days in liquid nitrogen, rapidly thawed, recovered for 24 h, and treated with pentamidine for 72 h. Viability was assessed in uninfected and PCP-infected PCLS before and after cryopreservation. Although post-thaw viability decreased in both groups, substantial viability was still retained, allowing further experimentation. qPCR showed that cryopreservation did not alter expression of the type I and type II alveolar epithelial markers podoplanin (Pdpn) and surfactant protein C (Sftpc) in either group. Importantly, pentamidine significantly reduced Pneumocystis mitochondrial small subunit (mtSSU) rRNA levels in thawed PCP-infected PCLS, demonstrating suitability for anti-Pneumocystis drug testing. These findings establish the first cryopreserved ex vivo PCP model using infected mouse PCLS, preserving endogenous fungal burden and infection-associated host responses while enabling flexible, scalable studies of Pneumocystis biology, host-pathogen interactions, therapeutic efficacy, and potentially other pulmonary infections.

candidates.title: Modelling Phenotypic Assay Noise for Multivariable Biomarker Discovery using Deep Neural Networks
candidates.abstract: Accurately predicting cancer drug response remains a major challenge in precision oncology. Although some therapies are guided by clinically-approved biomarkers, these markers often yield limited predictive value and are unavailable for many drugs. Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning approaches trained on large-scale cancer cell line pharmacogenomic screens offer a promising route to more comprehensive response prediction, yet they generally assume that phenotypic readouts are measured without error. This assumption is problematic because viability-based drug response assays are inherently noisy, potentially causing models to learn experimental artefacts rather than biologically meaningful determinants of sensitivity. Here, we show that phenotypic measurement noise is present in four widely used cancer cell line screening datasets and introduce Deep Concordance Index Networks (DeepCINET), a deep learning framework that explicitly accounts for this noise. Across datasets, incorporating this noise-aware ranking strategy improves generalization across experimental conditions and to previously unseen samples. DeepCINET outperforms baseline models in multiple settings, with particularly notable gains in prioritizing the most drug-sensitive cell lines. Together, these results establish phenotypic assay noise as a critical and previously overlooked source of error in drug response modelling and provide a principled framework for noise-aware multivariable biomarker discovery.

candidates.title: Optimization of mitochondrial membrane potential contributes to extended longevity of daf-2 mutants in C. elegans
candidates.abstract: Mitochondrial membrane potential is the charge difference across the inner mitochondrial membrane that is generated by the electron transport chain pumping protons from the mitochondrial matrix to the intermembrane space and is required for ATP synthesis, importing proteins into the mitochondria and movement of ions across the inner mitochondrial membrane. While a number of long-lived genetic mutants in C. elegans have been reported to have reduced mitochondrial membrane potential, increased mitochondrial membrane potential has also been associated with increased longevity. In this work, we examined the role of mitochondrial membrane potential in the long lifespan of daf-2 insulin/IGF-1 receptor mutants. We found that mitochondrial membrane potential exhibits a small but significant decrease in day 1 daf-2 mutants but a much greater decrease in day 8 daf-2 worms. We also examined the effect of genes and compounds that have been shown to alter mitochondrial membrane potential on daf-2 lifespan. Disruption of ucp-4, which increases mitochondrial membrane potential, decreased daf-2 lifespan without reducing wild-type longevity. Treatment with the mitochondrial uncoupling compound FCCP (carbonyl cyanide-p-trimethoxyphenylhydrazone), which decreases mitochondrial membrane potential, also decreased the longevity of daf-2 worms with no effect on wild-type lifespan. Combined, these results suggest that the altered mitochondrial membrane potential in daf-2 mutants contributes to their extended longevity and that their long lifespan is dependent on maintaining mitochondrial membrane potential within an optimum range.

candidates.title: The genetic architecture of lipoprotein(a): simplicity, complexity, and mutability
candidates.abstract: High levels of lipoprotein(a) (Lp(a)) increase risk of cardiovascular diseases. Lp(a) concentration is primarily determined (>80%) by genetic variation at LPA, particularly by its large, size-polymorphic kringle IV-2 (KIV-2) repeat. However, because variation of the KIV-2 repeat is difficult to measure, the precise ways that genetic variants at LPA and other loci determine Lp(a) levels have been unclear, especially in individuals of non-European ancestry. Here, we developed new computational techniques to accurately genotype KIV-2 variation in whole-genome-sequenced population cohorts. Applying these methods to UK Biobank (n=490,414) and All of Us (n=245,394) provided insights into the genetic determinants of Lp(a) and the mutational dynamics of the KIV-2 repeat, which we found expands or contracts intra-allelically once every [~]500 generations. Variation in Lp(a) levels among people of all genetic ancestries was accurately predicted by a single, transferable genetic model capturing cis-epistatic effects of KIV-2 length and protein-altering polymorphisms in LPA. Controlling for predicted effects of LPA alleles revealed an additional, highly polygenic contribution to Lp(a) variation: LPA-adjusted Lp(a) levels associated with genetic variation at over 300 loci (P<5x10-8), much like other blood lipids. These results elucidate the genetic architecture and mutational origins of Lp(a) variation, showing how detailed characterization of a largely monogenic trait can provide surprising insights for complex trait genetics.

candidates.title: A Stability-aware Computational Intelligence Framework for Risk-guided Corrective Decision Support in Execution-stage Routing Systems
candidates.abstract: Route disruptions require corrective decisions that respect what has already been served.This study develops a stability-aware framework that locks the executed route prefix and re-sequences only the remaining suffix, combining quantile travel-time risk, an adaptive metaheuristic search, and a route-stability term with an admissible unchanged-route option.Sixty-three daily instances were split into calibration and held-out subsets, the latter used only for evaluation.Daily-instance statistical analysis confirmed significant differences among the compared methods.The proposed method significantly reduced lateness relative to no re-planning while accepting higher lateness than free and risk-guided re-sequencing in exchange for greater route stability and fewer route changes.An adapted external adaptive-large-neighborhood-search comparator achieved lower lateness but with more than twice as many moved stops and lower route stability, and higher computational cost.A complementary fuzzy decision-activation gate, calibrated only on the calibration subset, retained most of the always-SA lateness-reduction benefit as a post-review robustness check.

candidates.title: Learning RNA secondary structure from chemical probing with MXfold2
candidates.abstract: Training RNA secondary structure predictors is limited by scarce reference annotations, even as chemical probing produces abundant nucleotide-level measurements. These measurements inform pairing states without identifying base-pairing partners. Here we extend MXfold2, which combines neural and thermodynamic folding scores, to learn from probing profiles and predict RNA secondary structures from sequence alone. We introduce three training objectives. One learns from probing-assisted target structures. The other two use implicit maximum-likelihood estimation to pass surrogate gradients from reactivity-ranking and likelihood losses through discrete folding. Simulations, RNAgym measurements and external structural tests show improved chemical agreement and gains in exact base-pair prediction when chemical supervision is combined with structural pretraining and replay. Probing profiles can thus broaden the range of RNAs that inform sequence-only structure prediction, including RNA populations with few complete structure annotations.

candidates.title: Adaptive tracking contributes to the invasion success of a global pest insect
candidates.abstract: Invasive species are a threat to biodiversity, natural resources, and the economy. Preventing future invasions requires the ability to predict which species will be successful invaders. Invading a new region often requires coping with novel environmental conditions, yet how invading populations adapt to environmental conditions encountered in their introduced range is not always clear. One process that may facilitate invasion in temperate environments is seasonal adaptive tracking, a rapid evolutionary process in which allele frequencies and phenotypes shift in response to seasonal environmental fluctuations, promoting the long-term maintenance of polymorphisms. Here, we test the hypothesis that adaptive tracking is a key contributor to the invasion success of the globally invasive fly Drosophila suzukii. We demonstrate that adaptive tracking results in predictable, rapid evolution of a key thermal tolerance trait (critical thermal minimum) essential for coping with climate variability. We also detect adaptive tracking in several genomic regions enriched for seasonally fluctuating alleles, and these alleles map to loci implicated in diverse traits, including thermal tolerance, pesticide resistance, and olfactory behavior. Finally, we find that loci undergoing adaptive tracking are significantly enriched for alleles associated with invasion in North American populations, suggesting that rapid evolution of seasonal traits may contribute to the success of this invasive species.
